subject: Confirming data-use constraints & model-tuning exclusion — post-demo recap
messages:

Subject: Demo follow-up — data handling & model-tuning confirmation

Hi Marta —

Thanks again for taking the demo earlier today. Quick recap and the specific asks we promised to confirm for your security/compliance team:

- You asked that AcmeWare data not be used to further train or fine-tune any public or shared Redwood models (i.e., a model-tuning opt-out).
- You requested retention and logging controls: 30-day request logs, 90-day access logs, and evidence of at-rest encryption for customer payloads.
- You asked about PII handling: automatic redaction options and whether we can filter or drop fields before persistent storage.

Next steps from our side: we can provision a binding configuration for your account that marks a "no-model-training" flag at the routing layer (prevents any training pipelines from consuming your data), and we will provide the Data Processing Addendum (DPA) and SOC 2 summary as attachments.

I attached a short SOC 2 summary and a draft DPA for your legal/security review (see attachments). Can you confirm the email address we should share the signed DPA back to and whether the 90/30 day log windows look acceptable?

If it helps, PrIyom can set up a 30-minute technical call with your security engineer to go over logging exports and redaction hooks.

Best,
Soojin

--

Hi Soojin —

Thanks for the thorough recap. A couple of clarifications from our side before we proceed with legal: 

1) Confirming: AcmeWare requires that our production data never be used to train, fine-tune, or evaluate models outside of a dedicated, account-scoped environment. We need that recorded as a contractual restriction.

2) Logging windows: the 90-day access logs + 30-day request logs sound reasonable, but can you confirm what fields are retained in the access logs (IP, user-id, request-id, model-id)? We want to ensure no payload fields are logged by default.

3) PII: We will provide a sample payload with PHI/PII fields. Can Redwood support a pre-ingest redaction hook so that fields marked by us are dropped before any cache or long-term storage?

We are looped in security@acmeware.com; they may ask for a short technical session. Please also confirm if turning on the "no-model-training" flag prevents any telemetry or aggregated metrics that could be used for model improvement, or whether we need an add-on for that.

Thanks — Marta
Director of Product, AcmeWare

Hi Marta —

Quick technical answers to the items you raised:

- "No-model-training" flag: when applied at the account level it disables any downstream training pipelines and excludes payloads from our model improvement telemetry (we also stop including your anonymized usage in aggregated quality reports). We will note this as a contractual control in the DPA language.

- Logging fields: Access logs will contain request_id, timestamp, model_variant, region, and originating IP (hashed on request if you prefer). We will not persist request payloads in access logs by default. Request logs (the request/response pair) are disabled unless explicitly enabled; for AcmeWare we will keep request logs off by default and only enable them with an auditable trigger.

- Pre-ingest redaction: we provide a webhook/redaction layer that can run a user-supplied redaction spec to drop fields before any cache/write. For production we can enable an account-side redaction config that never persists the dropped fields.

I'll flag a short technical call in Soojin's calendar; I can walk through the webhook schema and show how hashed IPs look in logs.

Regards,
PrIyom
Principal Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference

Hi Marta / AcmeWare security —

Thanks for the questions — summarizing the immediate commitments we can include in the DPA and account config: 

- Contract clause: Redwood will not use AcmeWare customer data for model training, tuning, or evaluation outside of an account-scoped (private) model, unless explicit written consent is provided. (We will add language to the DPA.)
- Telemetry: we will exclude AcmeWare from aggregated model-improvement telemetry by default when the no-model-training flag is active.
- Logs: access log fields are limited to request_id, timestamp, model_variant, and a hashed-originating-ip (we will not store request payloads).
- Pre-ingest redaction: we will enable the redaction webhook for your account; dropped fields will not be persisted to cache or long-term storage.

Next actions:
1) I attached the SOC 2 summary and a draft DPA — if legal is happy we can route the DPA for signature and apply the account no-training flag on signature.
2) PrIyom will host a 30-minute technical session with your security engineer (please propose 2 windows this week).
3) Once DPA is signed, we will apply the account config and send back a checklist of what changed in the console for audit.

Marta — can you confirm the preferred signer and the best email to send the DocuSign link to? Once you confirm I will send the DocuSign and Triaging will mark the account as "no-training pending signature" until executed.

Best,
Soojin
